items.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the definition of "for cause" revocation of licenses
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S4085

TITLE OF BILL:

An  act  to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
definition of "for cause" revocation of licenses

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL:

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1. Subdivision 3  of  section  118  of  the  alcoholic  beverage
control  law, as added by chapter 536 of the laws of 1996, is amended to
read as follows:

3. (A) As used in this section, the term "for cause" shall also  include
the  existence  of a sustained and continuing pattern of noise, disturb-
ance, misconduct, or disorder on or about the licensed premises, related
to the operation of the premises or the conduct of  its  patrons,  which
adversely  affects  the  health, welfare or safety of the inhabitants of
the area in which such licensed premises are located.

(B) As used in this section, the term "for  cause"  shall  also  include
deliberately  misleading  the authority on the nature of the business to
be operated on the licensed premises or changing the nature of the busi-
ness at the licensed premises during the licensing period without  seek-
ing prior approval from the authority.

Section 2 This act shall take effect immediately.

JUSTIFICATION:

The State Liquor Authority is in need of additional authority to address
the  growing problem of misconduct at the premises of license and by the
actions of those attending those premises.

This legislation will give the SLA the needed authority to quickly  deal
with  such  misconduct and deliberate misleading information provided by
the license holder.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

S. 5751 of 2015, Referred to Investigation and Government Operations

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT:

None

EFFECTIVE DATE:

This act shall take effect immediately.

A.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the definition of "for cause" revocation of licenses
A.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4085A

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the
definition of "for cause" revocation of licenses

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL :

To enable the State Liquor Authority (SLA) to revoke, cancel, suspend
or impose a civil fine on a business that obtains a license to sell
alcoholic beverages, for on-premises consumption, and the nature of
the business substantially changes in a manner that clearly and
substantially increases the incidence of local crime, nuisances or
disturbances and endangers the public health, safety and welfare of
the residents of the area where such establishment is located.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Alcoholic Beverage Control Law (ABC) section 118(3) is
amended to expand the definition of the term "for cause" to include
changes in a business' operations that are substantial, and which
endanger general health, safety and welfare of local residents, and
such changes in the operation of such establishment were not
contemplated when such application was approved by the SLA.

There are three ways in which the "for cause" criteria can be
triggered to start proceedings to revoke, cancel, suspend, or impose a
civil fine on an establishment.

1) The license applicant, when initially applying for such liquor
license, deliberately mislead the SLA as to the nature and character
of the business to be conducted on such premises.

2) the licensee, "substantially alters" the physical facilities of
such premises in a manner that greatly expands the size of such
business, and has not obtained the proper approvals as are now
required under state law.

3) the licensee "substantially alters the nature and character" of the
premises in a manner that condones the existence of a sustained and
continuing pattern of heightened noise, disturbance, misconduct, or
disorder on or about the licensed premises, related to the operation
of the premises or the conduct of its patrons, which adversely affects
the health, welfare or safety of the inhabitants of the area in which
such licensed premises are located.

Should either conditions 1, 2 or 3 come into being after the initial
license has been issued, then the SLA shall contemplate conducting a
hearing if such conditions or expansion in the scope of the business,
cause a significant increase in noise, disturbances, disorder, or the
commission of criminal activity that endangers those who live in the
area of such premises or who patronize businesses within such area.

A municipality or community board within New York City, may ask the
SLA to conduct a hearing to revoke, suspend, or cancel the license of
such licensee or impose a civil fine, if the nature or scope of the
licensed business greatly expands it operations or number of people
who patronize such establishment and that increased activity leads to
significant adverse quality life conditions for the neighborhood or
increases the danger to those who enter such area to patronize such
business or other nearby businesses. The SLA, after receiving such
municipal request, shall determine if the merits of the request are
bona fide and that a hearing is needed to consider revoking or
suspending such license. If the SLA determines that such a revocation

hearing is not required, then the Authority shall give an explanation
to the requesting municipality why such hearing was not conducted.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The State Liquor Authority needs additional authority to clearly
address the growing problem of misconduct at the premises of a
licensee that sells alcohol for on-premises consumption and by the
actions of those attending those premises.

This legislation will give the SLA the needed authority to quickly
deal with such misconduct and deliberate misleading information
provided by the license holder. Under current law, an applicant can
apply for an obtain a liquor license that the applicant maintains will
be operated as a local small tavern, however, upon being licensed,
greatly expands the scope of the business by utilizing the back yard
as a new bar area or highlights new evening entertainment attractions
that purposefully draws in clientele that that will disturb the local
neighborhood and substantially increase crime in such area. This bill
will give the Authority the tools that it needs to reexamine an
already issued liquor license to ensure that it is operating within
the confines of what the business represented itself to be.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

This bill has been substantially revised, so it is essence a new bill.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect 180 days after it shall have become law.

B.actClause: AN ACT to amend the alcoholic beverage control law, in relation to the definition of "for cause" revocation of licenses
B.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S4085B

 TITLE OF BILL :  An act to amend the alcoholic beverage control law,
in relation to the definition of "for cause" revocation of licenses

 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF THE BILL :

To enable the State Liquor Authority (SLA) to revoke, cancel, or
suspend the license of a business that sells alcoholic beverages, for
on-premises consumption, when: a) such licensee when applying for a
license deliberately mislead the authority on the true nature of the
business to be conducted, or b) the business activities of such
business substantially expands over time in a manner that clearly
increases the incidence of local crime or disorderly conduct.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :

Section 1. Alcoholic Beverage Control Law (ABC) section 118(3) is
amended to expand the definition of the term "for cause" to include
two new reasons to revoke, cancel, or suspend such businesses'
on-premises alcoholic beverage license.

Under this bill, there are two ways in which the "for cause" criteria
can be triggered to start proceedings to revoke, cancel, suspend, or
impose a civil fine on an establishment.

1) The license applicant, when initially applying for such liquor
license, deliberately mislead the SLA as to the true nature and
character of the business to be conducted on such premises.

2) the licensee after a license has been issued, "substantially alters
the nature and character" of the premises in a manner that
significantly enlarges the scope of business activities at such
premises and such activities significantly increase the amount of
criminal activity or disorderly conduct in the surrounding
neighborhood.

Should either 1 or 2 above occur or come into being after the initial
license has been issued, then the SLA shall contemplate conducting a
hearing if such conditions or expansion in the scope of the business,
cause a significant increase in noise, disturbances, disorder, or the
commission of criminal activity that endangers those who live in the
area of such premises or who patronize businesses within such area.

 JUSTIFICATION :

The State Liquor Authority needs additional authority to clearly
address the growing problem of misconduct at the premises of a
licensee that sells alcohol for on-premises consumption and fosters
civil disturbance and criminal activity by those attending those
premises.

This legislation will give the SLA the needed authority to quickly
deal with such misconduct and deliberately supplying misleading
information provided by the license holder. Under current law, an
applicant can apply for and obtain a liquor license that the applicant
maintains will be operated as a local small tavern, however, upon
being licensed, greatly expands the scope of the business by utilizing
the back yard as a new bar area or highlights new evening
entertainment attractions that purposefully draws in clientele that
that will disturb the local neighborhood and substantially increase
crime in such area. This bill will give the Authority the tools that
it needs to reexamine an already issued liquor license to ensure that
it is operating within the confines of what the business represented
itself to be.

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT :

None

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect 180 days after it shall have become law.
